title: Honey Lime Chicken Tray
seoTitle: Honey Lime Chicken Tray | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Glazed chicken with roasted peppers and red onion on one sheet
subtitle: Glazed chicken with roasted peppers and red onion on one sheet
description: Bone-in chicken thighs roast with bell peppers and red onion, brushed with honey-lime glaze until sticky and golden at the edges.

steps.title: Heat oven and prep vegetables
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss peppers and onion with 2 tbsp oil, salt, and pepper until evenly coated and lightly glossy.

steps.title: Season chicken
steps.instruction: Pat thighs dry. Season with chili powder, salt, and pepper. Arrange skin-side up on two half-sheet pans with vegetables around edges.

steps.title: Initial roast
steps.instruction: Roast 18 minutes without glaze until chicken skin starts to render fat and turn lightly golden at the edges.

steps.title: Glaze and finish
steps.instruction: Whisk honey, lime juice, garlic, and remaining oil. Brush over chicken and vegetables. Roast 10–12 more minutes until glaze bubbles and temp hits 165°F.

steps.title: Rest and portion
steps.instruction: Rest 5 minutes. Peppers should be tender with slight char; chicken juices should run clear, not pink, when pierced at the bone.

proTips: Watch glaze in last minutes—honey burns quickly above 425°F.
Serve with extra lime wedges for crew who want sharper acidity.
Swap thighs for drumsticks using same timing if that is what is in the walk-in.
leftovers: Slice chicken into salads with avocado and remaining peppers.
Shred into wraps with the sticky pan glaze as sauce.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Sweet-tart flavor wakes up a tired crew. One tray means less cleanup after a long shift.
mealPrepNotes: Mix glaze ahead in a jar. Line pans with foil for faster cleanup. Station: Brush glaze during last 10 minutes only—early application burns sugar. Station: Rotate pans halfway for even caramelization in a crowded station oven. Station: Rest 5 minutes before slicing so glaze sets instead of running off the tray.
